newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain bosses say union proposal slowing talks.
newsitem.headline: Spain bosses say union proposal slowing talks.

text.p: Spanish employers group CEOE said on Thursday that the latest proposal by trade unions was slowing down the ongoing jobs reform talks.

"The latest union proposal on the hiring of young people...represents a substantial slowdown in this effort to get (the two sides) closer," CEOE Chairman Jose Maria Cuevas told reporters before the third day of talks between bosses and unions.
Although the negotiations on how to make the labour market more flexible and curb Spain's high unemployment rate have made good progress so far, the two sides now differ over jobs for young people.
Unions want this type of contract to become permanent after the first four years but employers want the contract to expire after 10 years without any redundancy payment.
